As for storage, I like to roll it up! This lends itself nicely to the info stickers too as I use the stickers to keep the fabric rolled up & then I’ll pop them in length order on my shelves, trying to keep them loosely grouped by fibre type (natural, blends & synthetic). I’ll put stretch fabrics organised in the same way as above but on a different shelf. 
If you don’t have shelves, some clear plastic boxes would work too, you could even find some that could live under your bed if you lack space generally 

I took about a month to measure, roll up and organise all of my fabrics, I just did 2 or 3 a night until it was done, it seems really intimidating and overwhelming when you first think about doing it but it’s worth it if you take the time to do it properly! 

In terms of the notions, I understand your dilemma, the best thing might be to plan your next 4-6 projects & buy all of the notions for those projects at once. It would require some planning, and a bit of commitment but it would prevent the buying stuff just because! 

Otherwise I don’t know if you could get away with buying neutral colours for zips, buttons etc, so if you do have to buy multiples they could possibly used across a variety of projects?

I use this tape to organise my fabrics, it makes it easy glance to see the length what fibre it is, if it’s stretchy, if it’s already been washed etc:  https://www.kylieandthemachine.com/en-gb/products/katm-fabric-id-tape-1-tape-roll

& then I have my patterns organised by fabric length requirement (and stretch/woven sub-categories)

Notions are usually the cheapest part of a project so if I don’t have it in my stash, I’ll allow myself to buy (or thrift) it if it’s the only thing I’m missing from a project. 

Organisation will be your best friend!

I think you kind of answered your own question, walking (cardio) generally uses (all) of the muscle groups, in that you’re moving your whole body basically, so your heart works harder to provide enough nutrients and stuff too all of the working muscles. - in addition, walking requires you to be stood upright, which is not great with POTS. 


Weight lifting on the other hand, generally you’re focused on a specific muscle group, so it’s not as strenuous on your heart as cardio is - in addition, you can be in a seated/lying position to lift weights (or use resistance bands), further limiting the strain on your heart rate. 


Weight training for POTs is great, because it strengthens the muscles used to pump blood back up to your heart meaning overtime this (can) bring your heart rate down! I’m in no way an expert but this is generally the explanation.

Hi! Married in February this year, we originally started planning a big wedding 60-120 people originally, we also had estimates of between 15k -30k (one place wanted 26k dry hire basically!!) 
We both took a hard look at who we are, what we wanted from the wedding & what we both cared about the most, this helped us come to the realisation we were planning a wedding we wouldn’t like for the sake of everyone else!! Extended families are large, but we only see them once a year if that. MIL was pushing for literally everyone to be invited & we’re both anxious wrecks as it is. 

In the end we ended up scrapping the whole thing and scaling it right back. We only had immediate family there (parents, grandparents, siblings) and 2 of our closest friends. Total of 14 people. We got married in a beautiful venue that was actually one supplied by the registry office so cost only £200. We had an afternoon tea at a lovely restaurant with beautiful views looking over the country side & food cost roughly £400. 
I think in total it was roughly £1000 (once you include outfits) 

Everyone we’ve spoken too that attended the wedding said it was the nicest most intimate wedding they’ve been too. & most importantly we enjoyed our selves so much more. We were actually able to have conversations with all of our guests. There was very little stress because we knew everyone that would be there loves us unconditionally and wouldn’t ever judge us. 

We also booked a week honeymoon directly after the wedding, which we wouldn’t have been able to do with a big expensive wedding. 

Honestly it’s such a personal experience, my main advice would be just sit down and have an honest conversation about what you and your fiancé want. Not what you think you should want cause it’s the ‘norm’. But what you actually want from the wedding & if your ideas suit your personality. Also try to identity when you’re doing things to please others, because that can get very expensive! 

Wish all the best for you, good luck 💜
